changelog: First release of a multi-part backtest-realism series: making backtests behave like a real Bitfunded trade (same sizing rule, same costs) so results can be trusted to decide whether live trading resumes. This release is schema + session-setup fields only — the order ticket, the risk-ladder engine, and the running-trade display follow in v3.22.1-v3.22.3. Funding simulation was dropped from the whole series after calibration (below) found a single flat fee with no maker/taker split, so there was nothing left for funding to be calibrated against either — no funding_rates table, no Bybit funding backfill, no funding UI anywhere in this series.

Calibrated the backtest fee default from real data instead of guessing: 64 real Bitfunded fills on challenge 6 (source='import') all charge exactly 0.0400% of notional per fill, min=max=avg — no maker/taker distinction on this account. Hand-verified on trade 123: (6.4x782.51 + 6.4x766.07) x 0.0004 = 3.964, matching the recorded 3.9644. backtest_sessions.fee_rate_pct's DEFAULT changes from Bybit's generic, unvalidated 0.0550 to the calibrated 0.0400 for new sessions only — every existing session keeps whatever fee_rate_pct it already has stored.

New backtest_sessions columns (migration 2026_09_30_0001): default_leverage (1x/2x/3x/5x/10x/20x, NOT NULL DEFAULT 5 — the order ticket's leverage dropdown, shipping in v3.22.1, defaults to this per session and can always override it per order), risk_ladder_json (3 tiers as % of the session's own starting_balance, not absolute dollars — a backtest's starting balance is arbitrary per session, so a %-based tier is the only representation that stays meaningful across sessions), use_flat_risk (NOT NULL DEFAULT 1/flat — every existing session keeps its historical single-risk_pct behaviour with zero engine change; a brand-new session's own setup-form default is tiered, an explicit application-layer choice, not the schema's).

New Backtest form gains a Default Leverage dropdown, a Flat risk / tiered-ladder toggle (both the flat % field and the 3 ladder rows always stay in the DOM and are always both submitted — switching the toggle back and forth before submitting never loses either value), and a 'Prefill from challenge' button on the ladder that converts a real challenge's own risk_ladder_tiers (absolute dollar bounds) into % of that challenge's starting_balance via the existing get_risk_status endpoint — no new backend route was needed for this.

BacktestController::createSession() validates and stores all three new fields, falling back to a sane coded default (leverage 5x, the standard >=95%->1.0%/92.5-95%->0.5%/<92.5%->0.25% ladder) on anything missing or structurally malformed, rather than rejecting the request — the same treatment drawdown_type already gets for the same reason (an optional setup field, not a measurement where a silent default would misrepresent a fact). sessionSummary() returns all three new fields for every session, old and new alike.
release_notes: New migration 2026_09_30_0001_add_backtest_session_leverage_ladder_fee_defaults.sql — 3 guarded ADD COLUMNs + 1 bare MODIFY COLUMN (the fee default change), no MariaDB-only syntax. After Update Now, run migrate.php?mode=status then mode=run to apply it (in addition to, not instead of, whatever migrations are already pending from earlier releases). Next in this series: v3.22.1 (order ticket, replacing one-click Place Long/Short — also folds in the fee-charging engine check originally slated for a now-dropped v3.22.4), v3.22.2 (risk-ladder engine), v3.22.3 (running-trade chart display).
